D: policy_objective: Nepal's overarching five-year national development plan, covering every sector of the economy under the vision of 'good governance, social justice and prosperity'. In relation to plastics/waste, its objectives (spread across the Urban Development chapter and the Biodiversity, Climate Change and Green Economy chapter) are to: develop scientific, source-segregated integrated urban waste management with modern treatment/landfill infrastructure; discourage the use of plastic materials and prohibit the burning of plastics; make waste management cost-effective and sustainable through private-sector involvement, waste reduction, reuse and recycling; prohibit dumping of waste in streams/rivers or its burning in forests and open areas; impose a tax on waste disposed of in landfills; control plastic items; make producers, importers and polluters responsible for industrial, hospital and hazardous waste, implementing the concept of extended producer responsibility; and increase the use of green raw-material-based products in substitution for plastic products.
F: policy_target_text: "Discourage the use of plastic materials and prohibit burning plastics." (Chapter 7, Major Programs, Program 10 - Integrated urban waste management program). "Impose tax on wastes disposed of in landfills. Control plastic items." (Chapter 13, Major Programs, Program 4 - Pollution control program for healthy society). "Increase the use of products based on green raw materials, displacing plastic products." (Chapter 13, Major Programs, Program 1 - Green economy promotion program). These are plastics-specific commitments, but none is expressed as a quantified numeric target (e.g. a percentage reduction), so Column E is coded 0.5 rather than 1.
H: policy_type_justification: A national five-year development "Plan" (योजना) prepared and approved by the National Planning Commission/Government of Nepal (an executive planning body), not enacted by Parliament, and not a binding regulation in the legal sense -- it sets strategy, programmes and (per Chapters 7.6 and 13.6) quantifiable targets for the plan period. Because it does incorporate quantifiable targets (e.g. the 'modern integrated solid waste management centres and sanitary landfill sites' target, Chapter 7.6, item 8: baseline 1 (FY2022/23) -> target 17 (FY2028/29)), it is coded at the higher "Strategy/plan with quantifiable targets" tier (0.50) rather than the purely aspirational tier (0.25), even though none of its own quantified targets is itself plastics-specific.

L: policy_lifecycle_phases_list: production, consumption, recycling, disposal, environmental leakage
N: policy_budget_text: The Plan is implemented through Nepal's regular annual federal, provincial and local budgets and sectoral investment programmes (e.g. the urban waste-management-centre construction target in Chapter 7.6 implies dedicated capital investment), and Chapter 13's green-economy programme references green bonds, green finance classification, concessional loans and tax concessions for green enterprises, and payment-for-ecosystem-services/carbon-finance mechanisms (Chapter 13.6 quantitative targets: 'Issuance of green climate bonds', 'Payment for ecosystem services'). None of this constitutes a dedicated, ring-fenced fund specifically for plastics/waste created by the Plan itself, so this is coded 0.5 (funding sources mentioned, not ring-fenced for plastics/waste purposes specifically).
R: instrument_description: Chapter 7 (Planned, Sustainable and Resilient Urbanization and Settlement), Major Program 10 'Integrated urban waste management program': for scientific management of waste through cyclical use with source classification, extend technical support and construct necessary infrastructure; develop waste treatment systems including waste treatment centres and landfill sites in all cities; make arrangements for separately collecting biodegradable, non-biodegradable and recyclable wastes through local levels by developing separate management standards; and 'discourage the use of plastic materials and prohibit burning plastics.'
U: instrument_implementation_text: No specific implementing authority, enforcement mechanism, or monitoring process is named within this particular program description (those would fall to local levels/existing agencies under other laws); framed without an exemption (+0.25 unconditional).
W: comments: A five-year Plan describes a programme of government action for the plan period rather than enacting binding law in its own right; scored not-in-force (S=0) as an instrument of *this* document, even though 'prohibit burning plastics' is phrased directively. The corresponding quantified infrastructure target for this same program is coded separately below (Instrument 5) and IS scored in force, since it is the government's own numerically specific investment commitment.
